en: to be refused; to be rejected; to be denied

examples.en: My visa application was rejected.
My proposal gets turned down again.
I was once refused entry at a store.
I could not speak up, fearing I would be rejected.
I keep getting rejected, so I feel upset.
It hurts when a friend rejects you.

explain: '당하다'가 붙어서 내가 받아 주기를 바랐는데 상대가 안 받아 주었다는 속상한 느낌이 있어요. 단순히 안 받아들여진 일은 '거부되다', 상대가 내게 한 일로 느낄 때는 '거부당하다'를 써요.

phrases.en: I was denied entry at the airport.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나라에 들어가려는데 받아 주지 않을 때 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing for being refused entry into a country.

phrases.en: My friend turned down my request.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부탁이나 고백처럼 사람에게 안 받아들여졌을 때 일상에서 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: More common in daily life for requests or confessions turned down by a person.

phrases.en: I felt rejected by my friend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 속상한 마음을 말할 때 '기분'과 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with '기분' to express the hurt feeling.

explain_en: A person suffers a firm refusal from someone (환불을 거부당하다). The '당하다' ending adds an unhappy feeling that someone refused you when you wanted it accepted. A plain event of not being accepted uses '거부되다', while '거부당하다' feels like something done to you.

dis.h: suffer a firm rejection from someone
gh: a request is rejected, neutral and official

p.n: 거절당하다 sounds softer, like a request being declined.

examples.en: A firefighter rescued the child.
They rescue people who fell into the sea.

examples.ko: 산에서 길을 잃은 사람들을 구조할 거예요.
examples.en: They will rescue the people lost in the mountains.
The rescue took two hours.
I have rescued a stray dog before.

examples.ko: 다친 사람들을 무사히 구조해 줘서 고마워요.
examples.en: Thank you for rescuing the injured people safely.

explain: 위험에 빠진 사람이나 동물을 도와서 벗어나게 할 때 써요. '도와주다'는 일상의 도움이고, '구조하다'는 사고나 재난처럼 위험한 상황에 써요. 구조받는 쪽은 '구조되다'예요.

phrases.en: The child who fell into the sea was rescued safely.
phrases.nuance_ko: 구조받는 쪽을 주어로 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the rescued person is the subject.

phrases.en: There's a person here. Please rescue them!
phrases.nuance_ko: 위험한 상황에서 도움을 요청할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to call for help in a dangerous situation.

phrases.en: I'm raising the puppy that the firefighter rescued.
phrases.nuance_ko: 구조한 대상을 명사 앞에서 꾸밀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A modifier form for someone or something that was rescued.

explain_en: Rescue from disaster or accident by officials (소방관이 구조하다) Used when you help a person or animal escape danger. '도와주다' covers everyday help, while 구조하다 is for accidents and disasters. The one rescued uses '구조되다'.

dis.h: rescue someone from danger or disaster
gh: save from suffering or sin, deliverance
get someone out of captivity or a trap

p.n: 구출하다 stresses getting the person out of the dangerous place.

examples.ko: 사람이 많은 지하철에서는 소매치기를 조심해야 해요.
examples.en: You should watch out for pickpockets on a crowded subway.
A pickpocket took my wallet at the market.
I saw news that the police caught a pickpocket.

examples.ko: 여행 가기 전에 소매치기 조심하라는 말을 들었어요.
examples.en: Before the trip, I was told to beware of pickpockets.

examples.ko: 저는 어제 버스 정류장에서 소매치기를 당할 뻔했어요.
examples.en: I almost got pickpocketed at the bus stop yesterday.

examples.ko: 소매치기가 많은 곳에서는 가방을 앞으로 메요.
examples.en: In places with many pickpockets, I wear my bag in front.

explain: 피해를 입었을 때는 '소매치기를 당하다'라고 하고, 소매치기를 하는 사람도 소매치기라고 불러요. '도둑'은 훔치는 사람 전체를 부르고, 소매치기는 사람이 많은 곳에서 몰래 가져가는 도둑이에요.

phrases.example: 여행 중에 소매치기를 당해서 지갑을 잃어버렸어요.
phrases.en: I was pickpocketed while traveling and lost my wallet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 피해를 입은 사람이 자기 일을 말할 때 쓰는 가장 자연스러운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most natural way for a victim to describe what happened.

phrases.en: The police caught a pickpocket in the subway.
phrases.nuance_ko: 범인을 붙잡는 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone catches the thief.

phrases.en: These days there are many pickpocketing cases at tourist spots.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스나 안내문에서 일어난 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in news or notices to refer to incidents.

explain_en: When you are the victim, you say 소매치기를 당하다, and the thief is also called 소매치기. 도둑 covers any thief, while 소매치기 is one who quietly takes things in crowded places.

examples.en: The thief was caught and taken away by the police.

examples.ko: 아이가 낯선 사람에게 잡혀가는 꿈을 꿨어요.
examples.en: I had a dream that a child was taken away by a stranger.
In old tales, the bad people get taken away.

examples.ko: 그 사람이 왜 잡혀갔는지 아무도 몰라요.
examples.en: Nobody knows why that person was taken away.
If you do wrong, you could be taken to the police station.
After the criminal was taken away, the town became quiet.

explain: '잡다'에 피동을 만드는 '-히-'가 붙은 '잡히다'와 '가다'가 합쳐진 말이에요. 잡는 쪽이 주어면 '경찰이 도둑을 잡아가요', 잡힌 사람이 주어면 '도둑이 경찰에게 잡혀가요'라고 해요. 잡는 사람 뒤에는 '에게'나 '한테'를 붙여요.

phrases.en: The bad guy was taken away to the police station.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어디로 잡혀가는지 장소를 넣어서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use this when you say where someone is taken.
phrases.en_equiv: to be taken to the police station

phrases.example: 그 사람은 잘못이 없어서 잡혀가지 않았어요.
phrases.en: He did nothing wrong, so he wasn't taken away.
phrases.nuance_ko: 잡혀가지 않았다는 부정 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the negative form, saying someone was not taken away.

phrases.en: I almost got taken away on a dark road.
phrases.nuance_ko: 실제로는 안 잡혀갔지만 거의 그럴 뻔했을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use this when it nearly happened but didn't.

explain_en: It combines '잡히다' (the passive of '잡다') with '가다'. If the catcher is the subject you say '경찰이 도둑을 잡아가요', and if the caught person is the subject you say '도둑이 경찰에게 잡혀가요'. The person who catches gets '에게' or '한테'.

en: to come to invade; to come to attack

examples.en: The enemy suddenly attacked the castle.

examples.ko: 모르는 사람이 우리 집에 쳐들어와서 놀랐어요.
examples.en: A stranger barged into our house and I was shocked.

examples.ko: 화가 난 손님들이 가게로 쳐들어올까 봐 걱정돼요.
examples.en: I'm worried the angry customers might storm into the shop.

examples.ko: 친구들이 갑자기 쳐들어오는 바람에 청소를 못 했어요.
examples.en: My friends barged in suddenly, so I couldn't clean.

examples.ko: 게임에서 적이 우리 진영으로 쳐들어오고 있어요.
examples.en: In the game, the enemy is charging into our camp.

examples.ko: 옛날에는 이웃 나라가 쳐들어온 적이 있어요.
examples.en: A long time ago, a neighboring country invaded.

explain: 말하는 사람 쪽으로 힘차게 들어오는 것을 말해서 '쳐들어가다'와 방향이 반대예요. 전쟁뿐 아니라 갑자기 들이닥치는 사람에게도 써요. 딱딱한 말은 '침입하다'예요.

phrases.example: 적이 쳐들어올까 봐 마을 사람들이 무서워했어요.
phrases.en: The villagers were afraid the enemy might invade.
phrases.nuance_ko: 걱정이나 불안을 말할 때 '-(으)ㄹ까 봐'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with '-(으)ㄹ까 봐' to express worry.

phrases.en: A thief broke into the house in the middle of the night.
phrases.nuance_ko: 같은 뜻의 딱딱한 말로, 뉴스나 글에서 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A formal synonym often used in news and writing.

phrases.example: 친구들이 갑자기 방에 쳐들어와서 깜짝 놀랐어요.
phrases.en: My friends suddenly barged into my room, and I was startled.
phrases.nuance_ko: 친한 사이에서 갑자기 들어오는 상황에도 가볍게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Also used lightly for friends barging in.

explain_en: Same attack verb, but coming toward the speaker's side. It describes someone forcefully coming in toward the speaker, so its direction is the opposite of '쳐들어가다'. It is used for wars and also for people who suddenly burst in. The stiffer word is '침입하다'.

examples.en: The owner shut the dog in the yard.
They built an embankment to hold in the water.
You must not lock a child in a room.
The wizard locks the dragon in a tower.
Don't bottle up your feelings; try talking.
Where is the place where the criminal was locked up?

explain: '가두다'는 '~에 가두다'로 쓰고, 갇히는 쪽은 '갇히다'라고 해요. 사람, 동물, 물, 감정까지 쓸 수 있어요. '넣다'는 그냥 안에 두는 것이고, 가두다는 못 나오게 하는 거예요.

phrases.example: 강아지를 하루 종일 가둬 두면 안 돼요.
phrases.en: You should not keep a puppy locked up all day.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-아/어 두다'를 붙여 가둔 상태로 계속 둔다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: '-아/어 두다' means leaving it in the locked-up state.

phrases.en: I got trapped in the elevator and was scared.
phrases.nuance_ko: '가두다'의 반대편에서, 갇히는 쪽이 하는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The other side of '가두다', said by the one who is trapped.

phrases.en: Don't lock your sadness inside your heart.
phrases.nuance_ko: 감정을 밖으로 내지 않고 안에 눌러 둘 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for keeping a feeling inside without letting it out.

explain_en: 가두다 is used as ~에 가두다, and the one who ends up locked in is expressed with 갇히다. It works for people, animals, water, and even feelings. 넣다 just puts something inside, while 가두다 means making it unable to get out.

en: to topple; to fall on one's face

examples.en: I tripped on a rock and fell flat on my face.
The child was running, tumbled forward and hurt his knee.
The stock price is suddenly plunging.

examples.ko: 자전거가 급정거하자 몸이 앞으로 고꾸라질 뻔했어요.
examples.en: When the bike stopped suddenly, I almost toppled forward.
I was so sleepy that I fell asleep as if collapsing onto my desk.
The runner took a tumble right before the finish line.

explain: '넘어지다'보다 앞으로 푹 엎어지는 느낌이 강해요. 사람이 쓰러질 때뿐 아니라 주가나 실적이 크게 떨어질 때도 비유로 써요.

phrases.en: I almost fell flat on my face on the stairs.
phrases.nuance_ko: '앞으로'를 붙이면 몸이 푹 엎어지는 모습이 더 잘 보여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 앞으로 makes the face-first fall easier to picture.
phrases.en_equiv: to fall forward on one's face

phrases.en: The floor was slippery, so I nearly went down.
phrases.nuance_ko: 넘어질 뻔했을 때 '-ㄹ 뻔하다'를 붙여 자주 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used with -ㄹ 뻔하다 for a near fall.

phrases.en: The stock price plunged because of the bad news.
phrases.nuance_ko: 값이 갑자기 크게 떨어질 때 비유로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A figurative use for a sudden, big drop in value.

explain_en: Compared with '넘어지다', it strongly suggests pitching forward onto one's face. It is also used figuratively when stock prices or results drop sharply.

en: to bite; to chew; to gnaw

examples.en: The puppy chewed up my new shoes.
I have a habit of biting my nails when I'm nervous.

examples.ko: 고양이가 소파를 물어뜯지 않게 장난감을 줬어요.
examples.en: I gave the cat a toy so it wouldn't gnaw on the sofa.
The hungry lion tore into the meat.

examples.ko: 볼펜을 자꾸 물어뜯으면 망가질 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you keep chewing on a pen, it can break.
Please don't fight by tearing into each other.

explain: '물다'가 한 번 무는 것이라면, 물어뜯다는 이로 물고 잡아당겨서 떼어 내거나 찢는 거친 동작이에요. 동물이 물건을 망가뜨릴 때, 사람이 손톱·입술을 뜯을 때 써요. 사람끼리 심하게 비난하고 싸울 때도 비유로 써요.

phrases.en: When I'm nervous, I bite my nails without realizing it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이 불안할 때 하는 습관을 말할 때 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common collocation, used for the nervous habit of biting one's nails.

phrases.example: 강아지가 가구를 물어뜯지 않게 장난감을 줬어요.
phrases.en: I gave the puppy a toy so it wouldn't chew on the furniture.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동물이 물건을 망가뜨리지 않게 할 때 부정형으로 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form, often used when keeping animals from wrecking things.

phrases.en: The two candidates tore into each other in the debate.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람끼리 심하게 비난하고 싸우는 모습을 비유로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A figurative use for people attacking and criticizing each other harshly.

explain_en: Repeated biting that tears or chews, more intense (슬리퍼를 물어뜯다) If '물다' is a single bite, 물어뜯다 is a rough action of biting and pulling to tear something off or apart. It is used when animals wreck things and when people chew their nails or lips. It also works as a metaphor for people attacking each other harshly.

t90.ax: The puppy chewed up my new shoes.

examples.en: Careless driving leads to accidents.
I was careless and broke a cup.
I opened the door carelessly and hurt my hand.
He is sometimes careless with his words.
I lost points because of a careless mistake.

examples.ko: 약을 부주의하게 두면 아이가 먹을 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you leave medicine carelessly, a child could eat it.

explain: 반대말은 '조심하다', '주의하다'예요. '부주의하다'는 안전 안내문이나 사고 뉴스에서 자주 보이고, 사람에게 직접 쓰면 비판하는 느낌이 강해요. 일상 대화에서는 '덜렁대다'나 '조심성이 없다'를 더 많이 써요.

phrases.en: Careless behavior causes accidents.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 '부주의한'으로 활용해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Before a noun, it becomes 부주의한.

phrases.en: I was careless. I'm sorry.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자기 실수를 인정할 때 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: You can use it to admit your own mistake.

phrases.en: My younger sibling is not careful, so he often falls.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서는 '부주의하다'보다 이렇게 많이 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: In daily talk, people say this more than 부주의하다.

explain_en: The opposites are '조심하다' and '주의하다'. '부주의하다' appears often in safety notices and accident news, and said directly to a person it sounds quite critical. In daily talk, '덜렁대다' or '조심성이 없다' are more common.

t90.ax: I was careless and broke a cup.

en: to burn; to blaze; to be aflame

examples.en: A fire broke out on the mountain and the trees are burning.
The old house burned all night.
The blazing sunset dyed the sea red.
The ashes left after the burning blew away in the wind.

examples.ko: 창고가 불탈 뻔했지만 소방관이 불을 껐어요.
examples.en: The warehouse nearly burned, but the firefighters put out the fire.

examples.ko: 불타면 큰일이니까 난로 옆에 종이를 두지 마세요.
examples.en: Don't leave paper next to the heater; it would be serious if it caught fire.

explain: 불타다는 불이 붙어서 타는 거예요. '타다'만 써도 되지만, 불타다는 불이 크게 일어나 활활 타는 모습이 더 잘 보여요. '불타는 노을'처럼 붉게 빛나는 모습에도 써요.

phrases.en: The building is burning fiercely.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 불에 타는 중이라는 것을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it to say something is burning right now.

phrases.en: The blazing sunset is really beautiful.
phrases.nuance_ko: 실제 불이 아니라 붉게 빛나는 모습을 말할 때도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It can describe a red glow, not only real fire.

phrases.en: All the trees burned up in the forest fire.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-아/어 버리다'를 붙이면 모두 타서 없어졌다는 느낌이 강해져요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding -아/어 버리다 stresses that everything burned away.

explain_en: Something is burning with fire; also passion burning. 불타다 is to burn with fire. You can use '타다' alone, but 불타다 paints a vivid picture of a fire blazing. It can also describe things glowing red, like '불타는 노을'.

t90.ax: The old house burned all night.

examples.en: In spring, people pick mugwort in the fields.
My grandmother made mugwort soup for me.
Mugwort rice cake has a strong scent, so people either love it or don't.
The smell of mugwort fills the house.

examples.ko: 감기 기운이 있을 때 쑥차를 마셔요.
examples.en: I drink mugwort tea when I feel a cold coming on.
There is even ice cream made from mugwort.

explain: 봄에 캐서 국, 떡, 차로 먹는 풀이에요. 단군 이야기에서 곰이 마늘과 함께 먹은 것으로 나와요. '쑥'은 '쑥 내밀다'처럼 쑥 튀어나오는 모습을 나타내는 부사로도 쓰는데, 소리만 같고 뜻은 달라요.

phrases.en: My mother made mugwort rice cake for me.
phrases.nuance_ko: 쑥을 넣어 만든 떡이에요. 봄에 쑥으로 만드는 대표적인 음식이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A rice cake made with mugwort, a typical spring food.

phrases.en: I had a cold, so I drank warm mugwort tea.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말린 쑥으로 끓인 차예요. 몸이 안 좋을 때 마시는 따뜻한 차로 자주 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Tea made from dried mugwort, often mentioned as a warm drink when you feel unwell.

phrases.en: There's a mugwort smell in the kitchen.
phrases.nuance_ko: 쑥은 향이 진해서 '쑥 냄새'라는 말을 자주 써요. 좋은 향이라고 할 때도 있고 강하다고 할 때도 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Mugwort has a strong scent, so this phrase is common, either as a pleasant or a strong smell.

explain_en: It is a spring plant eaten as soup, rice cake, or tea. In the Dangun myth, the bear eats it together with garlic. There is also an adverb 쑥, as in '쑥 내밀다' (to stick out), which sounds the same but means something different.

en: to fall forward; to fall flat; to be turned upside down

examples.en: Yesterday I fell forward on the icy road and hurt my knee.
The child was running happily and fell flat on his face.
I tripped on a stone and almost fell on my face.
The cup tipped over and all the water spilled.
Be careful not to fall on the ice.
Since I fell on the stairs, I walk slowly.

explain: '넘어지다'는 쓰러지는 방향과 상관없이 쓰지만, '엎어지다'는 몸의 앞쪽이 바닥을 향해 앞으로 쓰러질 때 써요. 뒤로 쓰러지면 '자빠지다'를 쓰기도 해요. 컵이나 그릇이 뒤집혀 쏟아질 때도 써요.

phrases.example: 우리 집에서 학교까지는 엎어지면 코 닿을 데예요.
phrases.en: My house is a stone's throw from the school.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아주 가까운 거리를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say that a place is very close.

explain_en: General; falling forward, or an object turned upside down. '넘어지다' can be used for any direction of falling, but '엎어지다' is for falling forward so the front of the body faces the ground. Falling backward can be '자빠지다'. It is also used when a cup or bowl is turned over and spills.

t90.ax: Be careful not to fall on the ice.

examples.ko: 여름에는 물놀이 중 익사 사고가 늘어요.
examples.en: In summer, drowning accidents during water play increase.

examples.ko: 구명조끼를 입으면 익사를 막을 수 있어요.
examples.en: Wearing a life jacket can prevent drowning.

examples.ko: 아이들 익사 사고가 없도록 어른이 지켜봐야 해요.
examples.en: Adults must watch so that children do not have drowning accidents.
A report of a drowning came on the news.

examples.ko: 익사 위험이 있어서 수영장에 안전 요원이 있어요.
examples.en: There is a risk of drowning, so the pool has lifeguards.
Fortunately, he was rescued just before drowning.

explain: 보통 '익사 사고', '익사 위험'처럼 다른 말과 붙여 써요. 물에 빠졌다가 살았을 때는 '물에 빠지다'를 쓰고, 숨졌을 때 '익사'를 써요. 뉴스와 안전 안내에서 자주 보는 말이에요.

phrases.en: A drowning accident happened at the sea.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물에 빠져 사람이 숨진 사고를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for an accident where someone died in water.

phrases.en: The risk of drowning is high in deep water.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물에서 위험하다고 알릴 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used in warnings about danger in water.

phrases.example: 안전 교육이 익사를 막는 데 도움이 돼요.
phrases.en: Safety education helps prevent drowning.
phrases.nuance_ko: 익사가 일어나지 않게 한다는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means to keep drowning from happening.

explain_en: It is usually combined with other words, as in '익사 사고' and '익사 위험'. If someone fell in the water but survived, say '물에 빠지다'; '익사' means they died. It is common in news and safety notices.

examples.en: The door slammed shut because of the wind.

examples.ko: 누가 화가 나서 문을 쾅 닫고 나갔어요.
examples.en: Someone got angry and slammed the door on the way out.
Suddenly thunder boomed with a bang.
The car crashed into the wall with a bang.
The heavy box dropped on the floor with a thud.
I woke up startled by the bang.

explain: 크고 무거운 것이 부딪히거나 닫힐 때의 소리를 흉내 내는 말이에요. 같은 소리라도 '탁'은 가볍고, '쿵'은 무겁게 떨어지는 소리, '쾅'은 더 크고 세요. 보통 '쾅 하고', '쾅 소리'로 써요.

phrases.en: My younger sibling slammed the room door.
phrases.nuance_ko: 문을 세게 닫을 때 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing for closing a door hard.

phrases.example: 밖에서 쾅 소리가 나서 깜짝 놀랐어요.
phrases.en: I was startled by a bang from outside.
phrases.nuance_ko: 크고 무거운 소리를 명사처럼 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to name a loud, heavy sound.

phrases.en: The two cars crashed with a bang.
phrases.nuance_ko: 세게 부딪히는 순간의 소리를 나타낼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes the sound of a hard collision.

explain_en: Single loud heavy sound; door slam, crash, explosion. It imitates the sound of something big and heavy hitting or closing. 탁 is light, 쿵 is a heavy drop, and 쾅 is louder and sharper. Usually used as 쾅 하고 or 쾅 소리.

t90.ax: I woke up startled by the bang.

examples.en: My father saws wood in the yard.
I almost hurt my hand while sawing.

examples.ko: 나무를 반듯하게 톱질하는 게 쉽지 않아요.
examples.en: It's not easy to saw wood straight.
Please put on gloves and saw it.
The carpenter quickly sawed the board.

examples.ko: 주말마다 아버지와 같이 톱질하며 의자를 만들어요.
examples.en: Every weekend I make a chair with my father, sawing together.

explain: 톱으로 나무 같은 것을 자르는 동작이에요. 일상에서는 '톱으로 자르다'라고도 많이 말하지만 '톱질하다'는 톱을 앞뒤로 움직이는 동작 자체에 초점이 있어요. '톱질을 하다'처럼 명사 '톱질'과 '하다'를 띄어 쓰기도 해요.

phrases.en: I cut the wood with a saw.
phrases.nuance_ko: '톱질하다'를 풀어서 말한 쉬운 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easy way to say '톱질하다' in more words.

phrases.en: A man has been sawing in the yard since morning.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 '톱질'에 '하다'를 따로 붙인 모양이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The noun '톱질' followed by '하다' separately.

phrases.en: I keep hearing the sound of sawing outside.
phrases.nuance_ko: 톱으로 자르는 소리를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the sound of cutting with a saw.

explain_en: This is the action of cutting something such as wood with a saw. In daily talk people also say '톱으로 자르다', but '톱질하다' focuses on the back-and-forth motion of sawing itself. It can also be split as the noun '톱질' plus '하다', as in '톱질을 하다'.
